issues.description: Attribute name mismatch for the same conceptual fields: the problem statement prose asks for attributes named 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' (problem_statement.md lines 16-18), while the UML diagram in the same problem_statement.md (lines 63-68) and the solution implementation declare these attributes as 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (solution Lecture.java). This inconsistency between the prose and the UML/solution can confuse students about the exact field identifiers they must implement (and the expected constructor/getter/setter names and parameter order).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify attribute identifiers across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the problem statement prose (lines 16-18) to refer to 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' so it matches the UML and the solution implementation. Alternatively, if shorter names are desired, update the UML and solution to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' and adjust constructor/getter/setter names accordingly. Also add a short note in the task description that students should follow the exact attribute names shown in the UML.
